players.product: atomic force microscopes (AFM) for in-line metrology

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (consolidated, K-IFRS): Q2 2026 revenue KRW 53,038,561,979 vs KRW 52,309,189,062 in Q2 2025; Q2 operating profit KRW 4,216,571,167 vs KRW 11,966,820,237; Q2 net income KRW 2,592,730,125 vs KRW 4,048,386,140. H1 2026 revenue KRW 92,400,012,705 vs KRW 103,218,841,724 in H1 2025; H1 gross profit KRW 63,382,026,958; SG&A rose to KRW 57,067,379,236 from KRW 44,282,174,049 (R&D expense within SG&A KRW 11,885,793K vs KRW 9,045,333K; salaries KRW 23,139,075K vs KRW 16,585,402K), cutting H1 operating profit to KRW 6,314,647,722 from KRW 25,116,874,183 and net income to KRW 7,719,386,267 from KRW 19,002,056,936. Mix: the business overview puts H1 consolidated revenue at about 65% industrial AFM, 28% research AFM and 7% consumables and services, with exports about 92%; on a separate basis H1 sales were industrial equipment KRW 52,106,099K (68.25%), research equipment KRW 22,418,464K (29.37%) and consumables/services KRW 1,817,299K (2.38%). Consolidated revenue by location: Korea KRW 7,129,546K (H1 2025: KRW 12,928,432K), overseas KRW 85,270,467K (KRW 90,290,410K). Customers above the disclosure threshold (names undisclosed): customer A KRW 7,564,308K (8% of revenue) and customer B KRW 2,685,461K (3%), vs KRW 13,398,786K (13%) and KRW 11,436,045K (11%) in H1 2025. Average unit price of industrial AFMs (separate basis) rose to KRW 2,131,659K domestic and KRW 2,233,366K export in H1 2026 from KRW 1,655,714K and KRW 2,114,145K in FY2025. Separate-basis R&D spend KRW 14,147,533K = 18.5% of sales (13.8% in FY2025). FY2025 reference: revenue KRW 205,613,480K, operating profit KRW 42,191,026K.

Order intake and backlog (consolidated, KRW million): H1 2026 new orders KRW 141,276M (industrial KRW 95,978M, research KRW 36,624M, other KRW 8,674M) against deliveries of KRW 92,400M, lifting the order backlog to KRW 112,509M at 2026-06-30 (industrial KRW 85,880M, research KRW 22,452M, other KRW 4,177M) from KRW 63,633M at 2025-12-31 (industrial KRW 49,679M). The filing states the consolidated backlog was about KRW 102.3 billion as of the report date. No single order contract exceeds 5% of revenue. Customer advance payments (contract liabilities) rose to KRW 5,958,984K from KRW 3,743,327K at year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 orders KRW 141,276M (industrial KRW 95,978M); backlog KRW 112,509M at 06-30-2026 (industrial KRW 85,880M) vs KRW 63,633M at year-end

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex: H1 2026 production capacity 44 industrial AFM units with 43 produced (97.73% utilisation) and 98 research units with 97 produced (98.98%), vs FY2025 industrial capacity 78 / output 75 (96.15%) and research 272 / 265; production staff 38. PP&E purchases were KRW 45,425,934,640 in H1 (KRW 22,356,635,091 a year earlier) and KRW 90,443,746K of construction in progress was transferred to buildings as the new Gwacheon head office was completed; the head office moved from Suwon to Gwacheon in March 2026, with factory branches remaining in Suwon and Hwaseong. Inventory rose to KRW 61,187,589K (raw materials KRW 30,291,203K). In April 2026 Park Systems acquired 100% of Rocky Mountain Nanotechnology, LLC (Salt Lake City, Utah; probe production) to in-source components; subsidiaries Park Systems GmbH (ex-Accurion; imaging ellipsometers and vibration-isolation tables) and Lyncee Tec SA (digital holographic microscopes) are the other manufacturing units.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 industrial capacity 44 units, output 43 (97.73%); research 98 / 97 (98.98%); PP&E purchases KRW 45,425,934,640

quarterly_data.signal: Product and R&D pipeline per the half-year report: completed developments include the NX-TSH300 Overlay system for RDL process metrology in advanced packaging, the NX-Mask IR system for chemical analysis of photomask defects, the NX-Wafer Plus for wafer-bevel metrology (commercialised) and the NX-Hybrid WLI with high-resolution white-light-interferometer optics; development plans cover next-generation advanced-packaging process metrology, commercialising NX-Mask IR, a next-generation industrial FX system and Cu-pad inspection metrology, plus the NX1 ultra-high-resolution research AFM. The filing says NX-Hybrid WLI, NX-Mask and NX-TSH are generating revenue, with NX-Hybrid WLI orders and shipments under way from global semiconductor companies and NX-Mask supplied to global chipmakers and mask makers. Park Systems started a third joint development project with imec in April 2026 covering AFM use in advanced packaging, wafer bonding and related CMP, and is discussing expanding it. R&D staff 130.
quarterly_data.figure: NX-TSH300 Overlay (RDL metrology), NX-Mask IR, NX-Wafer Plus, NX-Hybrid WLI; third imec JDP from April 2026

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook in the half-year report: the company expects 2026 chip investment to keep centring on HBM, leading-edge logic and advanced packaging on AI server and data-center demand; it expects next-generation DRAM scaling and wider EUV adoption to raise demand for precision metrology and interest in its AFM solutions, and sees advanced packaging as a new growth opportunity. It plans to keep expanding R&D and cooperation with major chipmakers. The report cites MarketsandMarkets for an AFM market of US$541.8 million in 2025 rising to US$762.2 million in 2030 (industrial US$241.8 million to US$347.7 million), and states that the company believes the AFM market will grow faster than that forecast.
